classification.difficultyReason: Combine two sign conditions to identify a quadrant, then use the Pythagorean identity with the correct square-root sign. Part (c) additionally converts 0.7 to an exact fraction and forms cotangent from cosine and sine.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Name the quadrant in which $\sin\theta>0$ and $\tan\theta>0$ and hence find the exact value of $\cos\theta$ if $\sin\theta=\frac35$.

answer.worked:
Sine and tangent are both positive in the first quadrant, so cosine is positive.
$$\begin{align*}\cos^2\theta&=1-\sin^2\theta\\\cos^2\theta&=1-\left(\frac35\right)^2=\frac{16}{25}\\\cos\theta&=\frac45.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Name the quadrant in which $\cos\theta<0$ and $\tan\theta>0$ and hence find the exact value of $\sin\theta$ if $\cos\theta=-\frac45$.

answer.worked:
Cosine is negative and tangent is positive in the third quadrant, so sine is negative.
$$\begin{align*}\sin^2\theta&=1-\cos^2\theta\\\sin^2\theta&=1-\left(-\frac45\right)^2=\frac9{25}\\\sin\theta&=-\frac35.\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Name the quadrant in which $\sin\theta>0$ and $\tan\theta<0$ and hence find the exact value of $\cot\theta$ and $\cos\theta$ if $\sin\theta=0.7$.

answer.worked:
Sine is positive and tangent is negative in the second quadrant, so cosine is negative. Write $0.7=\frac7{10}$.
$$\begin{align*}\cos^2\theta&=1-\left(\frac7{10}\right)^2\\\cos^2\theta&=\frac{51}{100}\\\cos\theta&=-\frac{\sqrt{51}}{10}\\\cot\theta&=\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\\\cot\theta&=\frac{-\frac{\sqrt{51}}{10}}{\frac7{10}}=-\frac{\sqrt{51}}7.\end{align*}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Name the quadrant in which $\sin\theta<0$ and $\cos\theta<0$ and hence find the exact value of $\cot\theta$ if $\sin\theta=-\frac1{\sqrt2}$ and $\cos\theta=-\frac1{\sqrt2}$.

answer.worked:
Sine and cosine are both negative in the third quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\cot\theta&=\frac{\cos\theta}{\sin\theta}\\\cot\theta&=\frac{-\frac1{\sqrt2}}{-\frac1{\sqrt2}}=1.\end{align*}$$
